title: Browser based 90’s throwback shmup
author: Chatterlings
selftext: I built this mostly with gpt sol, I was impressed with its ability to generate consistent enough sprites for animation. Some assistance from claude/gemini also, in vscode. Link if you want to try it, free and just for fun: [https://gridloch.io/fortune-and-flak/](https://gridloch.io/fortune-and-flak/)

comments.author: crumbaker
comments.body: Could you elaborate on how you did the sprites/animations, and the background especially. Looks amazing.

replies.author: Chatterlings
replies.body:
Honestly nothing special prompt wise - I used GPT Sol in vscode to do the initial gameplay pass, and then told it to make scrolling backgrounds referencing mid 90s shooters, in parallax layers. As it was the same model building the game it understood the assignment and mostly iterated itself when the art wasn’t consistent, and I told it to otherwise. I find if you explain how and why it looks wrong it gets it. The main constraint was the maximum size it would generate - most stages here are three “player” level images, there was no easy method to get them to join appropriately. Thus the big sheds in the train level and some other elements masking the join.

Sprites were just “make a sprite animation sheet, kawaii shooter enemies from 1990s” and the specific instructions for specific enemies.

replies.author: Lordxb
replies.body: How did you overcome the temporal shimmer issue with multi image rendering?

replies.author: Chatterlings
replies.body:
I dunno.

GPT says:

Two different problems, and most people only find the first.

**Registration:** never trust the generator's cell grid — models drift the subject inside each cell. Repack locally against a real anchor (feet, coupler, weapon pivot), *not* the alpha bounding box, since the silhouette itself changes between frames and bbox-centring adds jitter instead of removing it. Automating it: take the **median** of every cell's bbox, not the union — union is hostage to one bad frame with a stray muzzle flash near the edge.

**Runtime:** round every destination coord to whole pixels, and make sure your atlas width divides evenly by its column count. Mine was 1210px over 4 columns = 302.5, so odd columns were sampled half a pixel across and consecutive animation frames aliased differently — the sprite crawled in place while animating.

And validate as an actual animation in-engine. Shimmer is a motion artifact, it's invisible in a contact sheet, which is exactly why it ships.
